title: Check: kubeadm bootstrap
description: Five questions on standing a cluster up.

questions.prompt: What does `kubeadm init` produce on the first node?

options.text: Certificates, kubeconfigs and static Pod manifests for the control plane

questions.explanation: It writes /etc/kubernetes/pki, the kubeconfigs and /etc/kubernetes/manifests, then waits for the kubelet to start the control plane.

questions.prompt: What must you do immediately after init before nodes go Ready?
questions.explanation: Until a network plugin is installed the kubelet reports NetworkReady=false and every node stays NotReady.

questions.prompt: Write the command that prints a fresh join command for a worker node.
questions.explanation: The original token from init expires after 24 hours; this regenerates it with the right hash.

questions.prompt: Where does kubeadm put the admin kubeconfig?
questions.explanation: The final lines of init tell you to copy it to $HOME/.kube/config and fix its ownership.

questions.prompt: Why does `--pod-network-cidr` matter at init time?

options.text: It sets the Service VIP range
Some CNI plugins expect a specific range, and it must match theirs

questions.explanation: Flannel's default is 10.244.0.0/16. A mismatch gives Pods addresses nothing routes.
